observation.visible_scene: A wooden table holds a large pyramid built from upright dark-blue dominoes, ringed by a curved trail of white dominoes. In the foreground sit a green plastic ramp/track, a small stack of flat boxes/cards, and two white rectangular blocks (one tall, one short) standing vertically at the pyramid's front base. Two windows and a patterned wall band form the background.
visible_changes: Frames 1-3 are static: the blue pyramid, the two white blocks, and the white perimeter trail all stand upright.
From ~t=0.2 the white domino line on the right begins toppling in a sequential chain, and the shorter white block starts tilting toward the green ramp.
By ~t=0.7-1.0 both white blocks have fallen/leaned down against the pyramid's front, lying flat over the green ramp area.
Starting around ~t=1.1 the front-left face of the blue pyramid begins to give way; blue dominoes tumble with visible motion blur.
The collapse spreads through the structure: by ~t=1.6-2.2 the pyramid degrades into a low, scattered heap of blue and white pieces, with the remaining standing height shrinking toward the back.
The green ramp, the stack of cards, and most of the outer white perimeter trail stay in place throughout; the camera and background (windows, wall) do not move.
The motion is object motion (toppling/collapse), not camera motion; the heap's spread is a collapse/deformation of the structure, not a translation of intact pieces.
outside_clip_unknowns: What first triggered the toppling of the white line and the white blocks (no operator or initial impact is seen).
The exact moment/cause linking the fallen white blocks to the onset of the blue pyramid's collapse.
The state after t=2.669 (whether the heap settles or more pieces fall).
uncertain_details: Whether the white pieces mixed into the final heap came from the structure's interior or from the nearby trail.
Precise contact relationships between the falling white blocks and the blue pyramid during the transition.
